2609.07989v1.adaptation: Test on NQ E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures signed order flow (buy/sell volume from tick data) rather than individual NASDAQ equities. This changes the claim from 'regimes in individual equity order flow' to 'regimes in index futures order flow.' Regime detection itself can proceed, but validation of regime persistence, economic significance, or trading utility will be limited by the 384-session sample size.
2609.07989v1.claim: Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection can identify structural breaks in signed order flow that separate periods of market stability from instability.
2609.07989v1.feasibility_reason: The core claim—that Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection can identify regimes in signed order flow—is testable on NQ futures tick data. However, the paper studies NASDAQ equities, and we have only one futures instrument, which eliminates any cross-sectional or comparative analysis. More critically, regime detection is typically validated on longer timescales or against external regime labels; with 384 training sessions, statistical power to confirm regime shifts and their predictive value is severely constrained.
2609.07989v1.title: Regimes in the Order Flow

2609.08060v1.claim: A logistic regression model combining exponentially-weighted team strength and draft covariates forecasts professional League of Legends map outcomes more accurately than dynamic Bradley–Terry and static benchmarks.
2609.08060v1.feasibility_reason: This paper is about forecasting esports match outcomes using team strength models and draft data. We have only NQ futures tick data with no team, match, draft, or outcome labels—nothing from League of Legends or any esports domain. The claim requires labeled match-level outcomes and team/draft covariates that do not exist in our dataset.
2609.08060v1.title: Pre-game paired-comparison modeling of professional League of Legends map outcomes

2609.08106v1.claim: Nyström low-rank attention approximates full cross-sectional attention in stock prediction and captures the learned attention structure's low-rank geometry.
2609.08106v1.feasibility_reason: The paper's central claim requires cross-sectional stock prediction on a universe of N stocks (N=300, 800, 3,500). We have only one instrument (NQ futures), so there is no cross-section to model. The attention mechanism, low-rank structure, and all empirical findings depend on modeling relationships *between* stocks; this is structurally impossible with a single futures contract.
2609.08106v1.title: Nyström Attention Matches Full Attention for Cross-Sectional Stock Prediction

2609.08581v1.claim: A reinforcement learning approach using reward-jump memory and stochastic return critics can discover profitable trading alphas more efficiently than baseline symbolic search methods across multiple equity universes.
2609.08581v1.feasibility_reason: The paper's core claim requires testing alpha discovery across multiple equity universes with cross-sectional evaluation. We have only one instrument (NQ futures), making universe-level generalization impossible. Additionally, the method's value depends on a large pool of candidate alphas and their comparative performance across assets—a cross-sectional problem fundamentally incompatible with single-instrument data.
2609.08581v1.title: AlphaRJM: Reward-Jump Memory for Stochastic Return-Guided Alpha Discovery

2609.08881v1.claim: Short-selling bans reduce liquidity and fail to support average prices, but effectively limit large drawdowns, with effectiveness depending on the share of informed stockholders.
2609.08881v1.feasibility_reason: The paper's central claim requires cross-sectional variation in short-selling restrictions across multiple instruments/countries to identify the causal effect of bans on liquidity, prices, and drawdowns. We have only one instrument (NQ futures) with no short-selling ban variation to exploit, and no ability to construct a cross-section of treated vs. control securities.
2609.08881v1.title: The Double-Edged Sword of Short-Selling Bans

2609.09405v1.claim: The Log S-fBM model reconciles rough volatility (H ≈ 0.1) with multifractal volatility (H ≈ 0) and exhibits small intermittency (≈ 0.02) across financial assets, with derivable scaling properties and tail distributions sensitive to H.
2609.09405v1.feasibility_reason: The paper is a theoretical statistical analysis of a stochastic volatility model (Log S-fBM), deriving mathematical properties, scaling laws, and hypothesis tests for the Hurst exponent. It does not propose a trading strategy or a testable empirical claim about price behavior that could be validated on market data. Testing would require either (1) fitting the model to realized volatility and comparing goodness-of-fit across instruments (cross-sectional), or (2) using the model's predictions to trade, which the paper does not develop.
2609.09405v1.title: The Log S-fBM model: Statistical analysis

2609.10407v1.claim: A Python package can reliably parse and reconstruct Uniswap trading and liquidity events from Ethereum transaction logs into structured trade and pool-state observations.
2609.10407v1.feasibility_reason: The paper is a software package for parsing Uniswap event data on Ethereum blockchains. We have NQ futures tick data with no blockchain, smart contract, or decentralized exchange components. There is no adaptation that bridges this gap.
2609.10407v1.title: dexamine: A Python package for Uniswap event data on Ethereum

2609.10865v1.claim: The Elliptically Optimal confidence interval for the difference between two independent binomial proportions is shorter than alternatives while maintaining coverage guarantees.
2609.10865v1.feasibility_reason: This paper is a theoretical statistics contribution about constructing confidence intervals for binomial proportions. It requires categorical outcome data (successes/failures in two independent samples) to test, but our data is continuous price/volume time series from a single futures instrument with no natural binomial structure.
2609.10865v1.title: The Elliptically Optimal Confidence Interval: A Bivariate Extension of Wilson's Score Method

2609.11614v1.claim: A deep reinforcement learning market maker augmented with regime-detection signals outperforms classical stochastic control market-making rules (Avellaneda-Stoikov, GLFT) under non-stationary order flow.
2609.11614v1.feasibility_reason: The paper requires bid/ask quotes, order book depth, and order-level microstructure data to simulate a limit order book and test market-making strategies. We have only trade-level data (aggressor side, volume) with no quotes, no depth, and no ability to construct realistic order book dynamics or test quoting rules.
2609.11614v1.title: Deep Learning of Robust Market Making under Regime-Switching Order Flow

2609.12227v1.claim: Seasonal trading models (DVR, SSA, RLSSA) applied to commodity futures with rolling estimation and transaction costs do not reliably outperform a buy-and-hold benchmark out-of-sample.
2609.12227v1.feasibility_reason: The paper tests seasonal trading across 15 liquid commodity futures contracts using rolling 10-year windows (2016–2024). We have only one instrument (NQ), making cross-sectional comparison impossible. Even if we could construct seasonal signals on NQ alone, the claim requires evidence of seasonality robust across multiple commodities with different harvest cycles and storage dynamics—a cross-sectional property that cannot be tested on a single equity index futures contract.
2609.12227v1.title: Seasonal Trading in Commodity Futures: Evidence from Regression and Singular Spectrum Signals

2609.12793v1.claim: A hybrid LSTM architecture using penultimate-layer vertical fusion of multi-scale temporal representations generalizes across multiple global equity indices and outperforms state-of-the-art models in price forecasting.
2609.12793v1.feasibility_reason: The paper's central claim requires testing on 10 global equity indices with 15 years of daily closing prices (a cross-sectional study). We have only one instrument (NQ futures) with 384 training sessions, making cross-market generalization and the comparative validation across 33 metric-dataset comparisons impossible. The claim fundamentally depends on multi-market performance.
2609.12793v1.title: VertiFuseX: Generalizable Financial Forecasting via Multi-Stream Temporal Fusion

2609.13402v3.claim: Diffusion models trained on implied-volatility surfaces generate coherent multi-period scenarios that, when used to optimize option hedges, reduce tracking error and tail risk compared to classical and data-driven benchmarks.
2609.13402v3.feasibility_reason: The paper's central claim requires implied-volatility surfaces and option-market data (SPX options, 2000–2023). We have only NQ futures tick data with no options, no quotes, no implied volatility, and no cross-sectional instruments. The hedging evaluation also depends on option prices and Greeks, which cannot be derived from futures alone.
2609.13402v3.title: Diffusion models for dynamic volatility surface generation and data-driven hedging
